name: Prometheus Tools
description: Prometheus monitoring tools for metrics querying and alert management

tools.name: PromQL Query
tools.description: Execute a PromQL query to retrieve current metric values

instructions.summary: Execute instant PromQL queries for current metric values
when_to_use: User asks about current CPU, memory, disk, or network metrics
User wants to check current service health or latency
User asks 'how is X performing right now?'
User wants a single point-in-time metric value
when_not_to_use: User wants historical data over time (use prometheus.range instead)
User wants to see trends or graphs (use prometheus.range)
User wants to modify alerting rules

output_interpretation.empty: Empty result[] means no data matches - verify metric name exists
output_interpretation.error: status: 'error' with errorType and error message explaining the issue

error_recovery.action: Check query syntax, verify metric names, escape special characters
Simplify query or increase timeout parameter
Retry once, check Prometheus server health

tools.name: Range Query
tools.description: Execute a range query for time-series data over a period

instructions.summary: Query metrics over a time range for trends and graphs
when_to_use: User asks about metrics over the last hour/day/week
User wants to see trends or patterns
User asks 'show me CPU usage over the last 24 hours'
User wants data for graphing or analysis
when_not_to_use: User only needs current/latest value (use prometheus.query)

tools.name: Alert Status
tools.description: Get current firing and pending alerts from Prometheus

instructions.summary: Check for active alerts and their status
when_to_use: User asks 'are there any alerts?'
User wants to check system health
User asks about problems or issues
Start of troubleshooting session
when_not_to_use: User wants to create or modify alert rules

tools.name: Scrape Targets
tools.description: Get health status of all scrape targets

instructions.summary: Check which targets are being scraped and their health
when_to_use: User asks about monitored hosts/services
User suspects metrics are missing
User asks 'what is Prometheus monitoring?'
Debugging missing metrics
when_not_to_use: User wants to add new scrape targets

instructions.summary: Query Prometheus for infrastructure metrics, alerts, and target health
when_to_use: User asks about CPU, memory, disk, or network metrics
User wants to check service health or performance
User asks 'how is X performing?' or 'show me metrics for Y'
User wants to see current alerts or problems
User needs infrastructure monitoring data
when_not_to_use: User wants to modify alerting rules (not supported via API)
User needs historical data older than Prometheus retention (typically 15 days)
User wants application-level logs (use log tools instead)

output_interpretation.success: Returns JSON with status='success' and data.result array containing metric values
output_interpretation.empty: Empty result[] means query matched no data - check metric name spelling and label filters
output_interpretation.error: Returns status='error' with errorType ('bad_data', 'timeout', 'execution') and error message

error_recovery.meaning: Invalid PromQL syntax or unknown metric
error_recovery.action: Verify metric name exists with prometheus.targets, check PromQL syntax

error_recovery.meaning: Query took too long to execute
error_recovery.action: Reduce time range, simplify query, or increase timeout
Retry once, then check Prometheus server health
Check network connectivity and Prometheus service status
